title: Define exchange parameter sets
action: Define the ferromagnetic (FM) parameter set: Jc=Jint=Je=J1=1, and the antiferromagnetic (AFM) set: Jc=Je=J1=1, Jint=-1. (Units: J=1 energy unit, kB=1).
description: Record the two parameter sets used in the computation. This step ensures the correct parameters are chosen before solving the EFT equations.

title: Compute ferromagnetic magnetization vs temperature
action: Solve the self-consistent EFT magnetization equations for the ferromagnetic parameter set (all J=1) with zero external field over a temperature range from T=0 to at least 3.0. Use root-finding to determine the four sublattice magnetizations and total magnetization at each temperature. Write the curve as a CSV.
description: Temperature dependence of sublattice magnetizations and total magnetization for the FM case.
output_schema: Header: T,mc1,mc2,me1,me2,MT. Columns: T (temperature in J/k_B), mc1, mc2, me1, me2, MT (total magnetization).

title: Compute antiferromagnetic magnetization vs temperature
action: Solve the EFT magnetization equations for the antiferromagnetic parameter set (Jc=Je=J1=1, Jint=-1) with zero external field over a temperature range from T=0 to at least 3.0. Root-find the sublattice magnetizations and total magnetization at each temperature. Write the curve as a CSV.
description: Temperature dependence of sublattice magnetizations and total magnetization for the AFM case.
output_schema: Header: T,mc1,mc2,me1,me2,MT. Columns: T (temperature in J/k_B), mc1, mc2, me1, me2, MT.

title: Compute ferromagnetic hysteresis loops
action: For the FM parameter set, solve the EFT equations with an external magnetic field H at temperatures T=1, 2, 3. Sweep H over a range that fully saturates the magnetizations (e.g., from -2 to 2). At each field value, record the sublattice magnetizations and total magnetization. Write all data to a CSV.
description: Hysteresis curves (M vs H) at T=1,2,3 for FM case.
output_schema: Header: T,H,mc1,mc2,me1,me2,MT. Columns: T (∈ {1,2,3}), H (external field in units of J), mc1, mc2, me1, me2, MT.

title: Compute antiferromagnetic hysteresis loops (all sublattices)
action: For the AFM parameter set, solve the EFT equations with external field H at temperatures T=1, 2, 3, sweeping H over a suitable range. Record all sublattice magnetizations and total magnetization at each field point. Write to a CSV.
description: Hysteresis curves (M vs H) at T=1,2,3 for AFM case, including all sublattices.
output_schema: Header: T,H,mc1,mc2,me1,me2,MT. Columns: T (∈ {1,2,3}), H (external field in J), mc1, mc2, me1, me2, MT.

title: Compute AFM central sublattice hysteresis at T=1 (fine grid)
action: For the AFM parameter set at T=1, solve the EFT equations while sweeping H with a fine grid (e.g., step ≤ 0.005) to resolve the triple hysteresis loop and peak effect region in the central sublattice. Write only H, mc1, mc2 to a CSV.
description: Fine-grid hysteresis for central sublattice at T=1, used to extract coercive fields and check peak effect.
output_schema: Header: H,mc1,mc2. Columns: H (external field in J), mc1, mc2.

title: Extract ferromagnetic key values
action: From the FM magnetization and hysteresis data, extract the critical temperature Tc, zero-temperature sublattice magnetizations, coercive fields at T=1,2,3, and whether remanent magnetization of central atoms exceeds that of edge atoms. Write these findings to a JSON file.
description: Summarized FM case properties: Tc, zero-T magnetizations, coercive fields, remanence ordering.
output_schema: JSON object with keys: 'Tc' (float), 'zeroT_magnetizations' (object with mc1,mc2,me1,me2,MT as floats), 'coercive_fields_T1' (float), 'coercive_fields_T2' (float), 'coercive_fields_T3' (float), 'remanence_central_greater_than_edge' (bool).

title: Extract antiferromagnetic key values
action: From the AFM magnetization and hysteresis data, extract Tc, zero-temperature magnetizations, coercive fields of total hysteresis at T=1 (Hc1, Hc2, Hc3), coercive fields of central sublattice at T=1, and whether a peak effect region (local maximum in |dM/dH| between Hc2 and Hc3) is present. Write to JSON.
description: Summarized AFM case properties: Tc, zero-T magnetizations, coercive fields, peak effect presence.
output_schema: JSON object with keys: 'Tc' (float), 'zeroT_magnetizations' (object with mc1,mc2,me1,me2,MT as floats), 'coercive_fields_total_T1' (object with Hc1,Hc2,Hc3 as floats), 'coercive_fields_central_T1' (object with Hc1,Hc2,Hc3 as floats), 'peak_effect_present_T1' (bool).
